proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord + magic_item kind in UnitRecord
proposed_widenings.justification: The surface type system has no magic_item kind. UnitRecord is SpellRecord | ClassFeatureRecord | MasteryRecord — there is no MagicItemRecord and the tracer has no handler for it. Every magic item is blocked at this boundary.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "Each of the quiver's three compartments connects to an extradimensional space" — this is a magic item, not a spell, class feature, or mastery.

proposed_widenings.name: passive_item_property mechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: The Efficient Quiver has no activation, no reaction trigger, and no on-hit rider. Its mechanics are always-on properties of the item (storage capacity, weight cap, draw parity). No existing mechanics family models a passive wondrous item property — all current families require an activation event.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "You can draw any item the quiver contains as if doing so from a regular quiver or scabbard." The storage is continuous and passive; there is no activation cost or trigger.

proposed_widenings.name: item_capacity (compartment storage)
proposed_widenings.justification: The quiver's three typed compartments (small/medium/long) with distinct item-count caps is a mechanically distinct construct. The v4 atom create_object covers conjuring objects, not modeling a persistent multi-compartment container with typed capacity limits. A new atom or surface type is needed to represent named compartments with individual cap values.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "The shortest compartment can hold up to 60 Arrows, Bolts, or similar objects. The midsize compartment holds up to 18 Javelins or similar objects. The longest compartment holds up to 6 long objects."

notes: Blocked at the record-kind level: UnitRecord has no magic_item variant. Even after adding MagicItemRecord, a passive_item_property family and a compartment-storage atom would be required. The draw-parity clause ('as if from a regular quiver') is a null mechanic — no special handling needed once the storage model exists. Weight normalization (always 2 lbs) is a secondary property that might fit a future modify_weight atom or be treated as flavor metadata.
